statement: Late time-restricted eating (16:8) produces only small weight loss that is not significantly greater than a non-restricted control eating schedule, and a notable fraction of the lost weight is lean mass.
effect_size: Modest weight loss (~1 kg) not different from control; significant proportion lean mass.
population: 116 adults with overweight/obesity, 12-week RCT (TREAT)

provenance.primary: Lowe DA et al., 'Effects of Time-Restricted Eating... TREAT Randomized Clinical Trial', JAMA Intern Med 2020

confidence_notes: Single RCT; late window is the weakest TRE variant. Grade: MODERATE — benefit is the deficit/adherence, not the clock.

statement: Early time-restricted eating (6-hour early window, isocaloric, no weight loss) improves insulin sensitivity, blood pressure, and oxidative-stress markers — a genuine circadian, weight-independent effect.
effect_size: Improved insulin sensitivity, beta-cell responsiveness, BP; isocaloric (no weight change).
population: 8 men with prediabetes, randomized crossover (small)

provenance.primary: Sutton EF, Peterson CM et al., 'Early Time-Restricted Feeding Improves Insulin Sensitivity...', Cell Metab 2018

confidence_notes: Tiny n, short, but tightly controlled (isocaloric) — the cleanest evidence that TIMING (early) matters beyond calories. Grade: MODERATE+.

statement: Alternate-day fasting produces weight loss and cardiometabolic change no better than daily continuous calorie restriction, with higher dropout and no preferential sparing of lean mass.
effect_size: Weight loss ~6% at 6 months, equal to daily CR; higher attrition in ADF arm.
population: 100 adults, 1-year RCT (ADF vs daily CR vs control)

provenance.primary: Trepanowski JF et al., 'Effect of Alternate-Day Fasting...', JAMA Intern Med 2017

confidence_notes: Deflates the 'ADF is metabolically special' claim. Grade: MODERATE (= continuous restriction).

statement: The 5:2 diet (two ~500-600 kcal days per week) achieves weight loss and metabolic improvement comparable to, not greater than, daily continuous energy restriction; it is a delivery format for a weekly deficit.
effect_size: Intermittent vs continuous energy restriction: similar weight and cardiometabolic outcomes across meta-analyses.
population: Meta-analyses of intermittent vs continuous energy restriction RCTs

provenance.primary: Multiple meta-analyses of intermittent vs continuous energy restriction (e.g. MASLD SR/meta, Front Nutr 2026)
provenance.surfaced_via: Europe PMC (intermittent vs continuous energy restriction)

confidence_notes: Choose by adherence preference. Grade: MODERATE (= CR).

statement: One-meal-a-day (OMAD) eating has only thin human evidence (case reports, small studies); isocaloric single-meal eating can raise fasting glucose, morning cortisol, and blood pressure versus multiple meals.
effect_size: Case-level weight/glycemic improvement in deficit; crossover signals of raised fasting glucose/cortisol.
population: Case reports and small crossover studies

provenance.primary: OMAD prediabetes/obesity case management, J Family Med Prim Care 2025; older single-meal crossover physiology

confidence_notes: Extreme TRE; nutrient/protein adequacy hard to hit in one meal. Grade: WEAK.

statement: Intermittent fasting patterns that cluster protein into fewer boluses (especially ADF and OMAD) can blunt the per-meal anabolic signal; without high protein (~1.6 g/kg) and resistance training, a larger share of weight lost is lean mass.
effect_size: Greater lean-mass loss risk vs evenly-distributed protein; mitigated by protein + resistance training.
population: Inference from leucine-threshold MPS physiology + IF body-composition data

provenance.primary: Leucine-threshold MPS literature (cross-ref 03-nutrition-supplements.md §2.2); IF body-composition trials

confidence_notes: Mechanism + supportive trial signal; the most important practical caveat for IF. Grade: real caveat.

statement: Prolonged periodic (Buchinger ~200-250 kcal/day) fasting of 4-21 days improved weight, blood pressure, lipids, and glycemia with good tolerability in a large observational series — but the study has no control group, so benefit cannot be cleanly attributed to fasting per se.
effect_size: Weight/BP/lipid/glucose improvements; few serious adverse events across 1422 subjects.
population: 1422 subjects (BP analysis 1610), single-arm observational, Buchinger Wilhelmi clinic

provenance.primary: Wilhelmi de Toledo F et al., 'Safety, health improvement and well-being during a 4 to 21-day fasting period...', PLoS One 2019

confidence_notes: Uncontrolled, self-selected, supervised. Directional safety/effect signal, not causal proof. Grade: WEAK-MODERATE.

statement: Medically supervised water-only fasting (Goldhamer / TrueNorth) followed by a whole-plant-food diet is associated with reductions in blood pressure and Lp(a) and favorable metabolic shifts in single-arm case series.
effect_size: BP and Lp(a) reductions; metabolic improvement post-fast + whole-plant-food diet.
population: Supervised single-arm case series, TrueNorth Health Center

provenance.primary: Reduction in Lp(a) after a medically supervised, prolonged water-only fast, Front Nutr 2024; Nutrients 2024

confidence_notes: Single-arm, supervised, self-selected, includes refeeding protocol. Grade: WEAK (supervised-only).

statement: Refeeding syndrome — acute hypophosphatemia/hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia and fluid shifts on reintroducing nutrition (especially carbohydrate) after prolonged fasting/starvation — is a genuine, potentially fatal danger; documented harms include arrhythmia, seizures, and (with thiamine depletion) Wernicke's encephalopathy.
effect_size: Refeeding hypophosphatemia incidence/mortality measurable in critically ill; case reports of severe outcomes after long self-directed fasts.
population: Critically ill/malnourished cohorts + fasting case reports

provenance.primary: Refeeding-syndrome incidence/mortality SR/meta, Sci Rep 2026; Wernicke's after 40-day water fast, Clin Case Rep 2026

confidence_notes: The genuinely dangerous part of extended fasting; mandates slow, thiamine-supplemented, monitored refeed. Grade: real hazard.

statement: The dry-fasting claim that 'one day of dry fasting equals three days of water fasting' has no human evidence; withholding water drives dehydration and raises risk of acute kidney injury, stones, hypernatremia, and thrombosis (Ramadan/CKD data).
effect_size: No evidence for the 1:3 ratio; elevated renal risk in CKD and with heat/long fasting hours.
population: Ramadan cohorts incl. chronic kidney disease patients

provenance.primary: Ramadan Fasting and Its Impact on Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease, Cureus 2024; heat + prolonged fasting nephrology, Int J Nephrol 2023

confidence_notes: Claim unsupported; harm mechanistically obvious. Grade: WEAK-EVIDENCE + POTENTIALLY-HARMFUL — not endorsed.

statement: The fasting-mimicking diet (FMD/ProLon, Longo) run as 3 monthly 5-day cycles improved body weight, blood pressure, fasting glucose, IGF-1, and CRP in a human RCT, with the largest effects in higher-risk participants — but outcomes are surrogate markers, trials are short, and the work is commercially entangled.
effect_size: Improved weight, BP, fasting glucose, IGF-1, CRP after 3 monthly cycles; biological-age estimate reductions in later analyses.
population: ~100 generally healthy adults, randomized (Wei 2017)

provenance.primary: Wei M et al. (Longo group), 'Fasting-mimicking diet and markers/risk factors for aging, diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular disease', Sci Transl Med 2017

confidence_notes: Best-evidenced branded protocol; surrogate-level, short, COI (Longo foundation/product). Mechanism: Brandhorst 2015 Cell Metab 10.1016/j.cmet.2015.05.012. Grade: MODERATE.

statement: Popular fasting-autophagy timing claims (e.g. '16h triggers, 24h maximizes autophagy') are extrapolated from rodent and cell studies; human autophagy flux is hard to measure, autophagy is also induced by exercise/sleep/CR/spermidine, and no human study establishes a fasting clock or a resulting health outcome.
effect_size: Fasting plausibly increases human autophagy (inferred); specific hour-thresholds and uniqueness are unsupported; outcome undemonstrated.
population: Rodent/in-vitro mechanism; indirect human surrogate markers only

provenance.primary: Ohsumi autophagy machinery (Nobel 2016, cross-ref 01-foundations.md §3.2); human autophagy-measurement limitations literature
provenance.surfaced_via: domain synthesis + Europe PMC (autophagy fasting humans)

confidence_notes: Autophagy is foundation-tier real; the marketed dose-response is mechanism over-extended into outcome. Grade: WEAK / mechanism-over-extended.

statement: The Master Cleanse (lemon/maple/cayenne liquid fast, Stanley Burroughs) has no evidence for 'detox' or disease cure; it is a protein-free very-low-calorie crash diet whose weight loss is the deficit and is reliably regained.
effect_size: No detox effect; transient deficit-driven weight loss skewed to water/glycogen/lean mass.
population: No controlled human evidence

provenance.primary: Detox-diet critical reviews (no quality evidence for detox concept), e.g. Klein & Kiat, J Hum Nutr Diet 2015

confidence_notes: Cross-ref liver-detox debunk 17-organ-systems-atlas.md §3.5. Grade: PSEUDOSCIENCE (detox) / crash diet.

statement: Juice cleanses have no detox evidence; they strip fiber, concentrate sugar, provide near-zero protein, and any weight loss is a rebounding deficit. Whole vegetables and fruit are superior on every axis.
effect_size: No detox effect; glycemic load; no nutritional advantage over whole foods.
population: No controlled human evidence

provenance.primary: Detox-diet critical reviews; whole-food vs juice nutrition

confidence_notes: Risky in diabetes (sugar) and CKD (potassium); unpasteurized juice infection risk. Grade: PSEUDOSCIENCE (detox).

statement: Colon cleanses / colonic hydrotherapy to remove 'impacted waste' or 'mucoid plaque' have no evidence of benefit ('mucoid plaque' is not a real anatomical entity) and a documented record of harm: electrolyte disturbance, infection, bowel perforation, and deaths.
effect_size: No benefit; documented serious harms (perforation, electrolyte deaths, infection).
population: Case reports / adverse-event literature

provenance.primary: Coffee-enema / colon-cleanse adverse-event literature (cross-ref 32-biohacking-fringe.md §6.3); colonic hydrotherapy complication reports

confidence_notes: Distinct from legitimate medical bowel prep before colonoscopy. Grade: PSEUDOSCIENCE + POTENTIALLY-HARMFUL.

statement: The 'stones' passed after an olive-oil-and-citrus liver/gallbladder flush are saponified fatty-acid soap complexes formed in the gut, not gallstones or 'liver stones'; the flush cannot clear the biliary tree and the claim is debunked.
effect_size: Chemical analysis: passed 'stones' = saponified oil, no cholesterol/bile-stone constituents.
population: Chemical analysis of passed material (Lancet 2005 letter)

provenance.primary: Sies H, Brinkmann J, 'Liver cleansing reports' / analysis showing saponified oil, The Lancet 2005

confidence_notes: Epsom-salt purge causes dehydration; can dislodge a real stone into the bile duct. Grade: PSEUDOSCIENCE (debunked).

statement: Parasite cleanses rest on a false premise that most people in developed settings harbor symptomatic parasites; 'ropeworms' shown as evidence are sloughed intestinal mucus/epithelium, not organisms. Real parasitic infection is diagnosed and treated with specific drugs.
effect_size: No benefit; 'ropeworms' = intestinal mucus/lining.
population: No controlled evidence; parasitology baseline

provenance.primary: Parasitology consensus that 'ropeworms' are sloughed mucosa; diagnosis-and-treat standard of care

confidence_notes: Real danger = herbal toxicity (thujone), unsafe self-dosed antiparasitics, and missing a true diagnosis. Grade: PSEUDOSCIENCE.

statement: Marketed 'detox'/teatox teas produce apparent weight loss largely through undisclosed laxatives (often senna) and diuretics causing water loss, with no detox evidence; chronic use causes laxative dependence and electrolyte loss.
effect_size: Water loss from hidden senna/diuretics, not fat loss; no detox effect.
population: Mini-review of diet/detox teas

provenance.primary: 'Safety and effectiveness of diet and detox teas for weight loss: a mini-review', Front Nutr 2026

confidence_notes: Hypokalemia (cardiac) risk; dangerous overlap with eating-disorder purging. Grade: PSEUDOSCIENCE + POTENTIALLY-HARMFUL.

statement: The Snake Diet (Cole Robinson) pairs a valid kernel — electrolytes ('snake juice': sodium/potassium/magnesium) genuinely matter during extended fasting — with an unsafe, evidence-free program of extreme recurrent fasting and anti-medical, 'fasting cures everything' messaging.
effect_size: Electrolyte component real; program weight loss is the (often excessive) deficit; no trial base for the program.
population: No controlled evidence for the program

provenance.primary: Extended-fasting electrolyte physiology (real kernel); Snake Diet program description (no trial base)

confidence_notes: Anti-medical framing discourages supervision exactly where extended fasting needs it; disordered-eating risk. Grade: MIXED.

statement: Self-directed fasts beyond ~24-48 hours warrant medical input and beyond ~72 hours should be supervised with electrolyte monitoring and a planned refeed; the benign safety record of clinic fasting series reflects the supervision and screening, not the duration alone.
effect_size: Conservative supervision threshold derived from refeeding/electrolyte risk and clinical practice.
population: Clinical practice synthesis + supervised fasting series

provenance.primary: International consensus on fasting terminology, Cell Metab 2024; Buchinger/Goldhamer supervised protocols

confidence_notes: Practice-based safety guidance, not a trial result. Grade: prudent default.

statement: Fasting is contraindicated or requires medical supervision in: type 1 diabetes and any diabetic on insulin/sulfonylureas (hypoglycemia/DKA; SGLT2i euglycemic DKA), pregnancy/breastfeeding, eating-disorder history, underweight/frail/older-sarcopenic adults, children/adolescents, certain medications (diuretics, narrow-therapeutic-window drugs), and advanced kidney/liver disease.
effect_size: Defined exclusion set with mechanistic harm rationale (hypoglycemia, DKA, muscle loss, ED reactivation, electrolyte/fluid risk).
population: Clinical risk synthesis

provenance.primary: Diabetes/fasting safety guidance; eating-disorder and sarcopenia literature; refeeding/electrolyte physiology

confidence_notes: The load-bearing safety box of the chapter. Grade: established clinical guidance.
